With 90 seconds per run and 4 in parallel, this is manageable, especially since backward pass dominates step time and there's no real need to optimize further. Time to calibrate the synthetic separation and kick off the large-n simulation.

I'll settle on sep=0.38 and simulate at n=80000 with 20000 steps across a weight-decay grid, running one seed each in parallel to keep things fast. I'll also queue up the real-data selection test at 4000, which is already prepared to launch.

I want a reference point for the synthetic experiments, so I'll recompute the Bayes-optimal accuracy from the same generative model parameters — I just need to regenerate mu and cov since make() uses a fixed generator, so I'll replicate that logic directly in the script.

input.command:
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 && cat > bigsim.py <<'EOF'
import sys, json, numpy as np, time; sys.path.insert(0,'/app/repo'); import train as T; from synth import make
BASE=json.load(open('/app/repo/config.json'))
sep=float(sys.argv[1]); wds=[float(w) for w in sys.argv[2].split(',')]; n=int(sys.argv[3]); steps=int(sys.argv[4])
X,y,yg=make(n,1,sep=sep); Xd,_,yd=make(10000,999,sep=sep)
for wd in wds:
    c=dict(BASE); c['weight_decay']=wd; t0=time.time(); P,norm=T.train(X,y,steps,c,seed=0)
    ptr=T.predict(P,norm,X[:10000])
    print('sep %.2f n %d steps %d wd %.2f  gold-test %.4f  train-crowd %.3f train-gold %.3f  %.0fs'%(sep,n,steps,wd,(T.predict(P,norm,Xd)==yd).mean(),(ptr==y[:10000]).mean(),(ptr==yg[:10000]).mean(),time.time()-t0),flush=True)
EOF
python3 bigsim.py 0.38 0.03,3.0 80000 20000 > big_a.log &
python3 bigsim.py 0.38 0.1,1.0 80000 20000 > big_b.log &
python3 bigsim.py 0.38 0.3,10.0 80000 20000 > big_c.log &
python3 bigsim.py 0.38 0.3,1.0,3.0,5.0 4000 1000 > small_d.log &
wait; cat small_d.log big_a.log big_b.log big_c.log
